Student worker – AI & Finance

Are you passionate about making a difference in the world through innovative BioSolutions?

ALGIECEL is a BioSolutions company on a mission to deliver sustainable, high-quality ingredients at scale – meeting the growing global demand without pressuring our planet’s ecosystem. Harnessing nature’s own way and putting it to use at industrial scale, we grow microalgae using light and CO2 in modular photobioreactors.

With the way we feed the world today, we are overexploiting planetary boundaries. There is a critical need for reliable partners who can translate innovation into industrial capacity for sustainable ingredients at scale. ALGIECEL provides an alternative with low CO2, water and land use, for customers that want to decarbonize their value chain.

You will play an important role in helping us drive the daily challenges of a start-up, with hands-on learning experience in AI, operations, finance & fundraising, as well as project management and engagement with the company’s leadership team and relevant external stakeholders.

We are looking for someone who can catch a lot of tasks and execute with quality those that matter. This role is perfect for a motivated student eager to step into a dynamic and fast paced work environment with high diversity of learning- and career development opportunities.

WHO ARE YOU?

• You are a 1st year master student based in Copenhagen, with studies in business, finance or Data/AI/Automation

• You are top of your class and consider yourself a high achiever among your peers.

• You have excellent written and verbal English skills (Danish is not a requirement)

• You have relevant work experience, as well as international experience.

WHAT WILL YOUR TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES BE AT ALGIECEL?

• You will drive the standardization and automation of existing operational workstreams in the company, while developing the company's AI toolbox.

• You will apply the above as well to support internal financial reporting to management and other relevant stakeholders.

• You will support and drive efforts to increase adoption of AI tools across the diverse team, as well as explore and execute use cases in parallel.

• You will participate in efforts related to fundraising for public grants, as well as equity rounds.

• Further, there will be ad hoc tasks and project, generally in support and collaboration of the company's Chief of Staff as your direct manager, as well as to the CEO and CFO.

HOW WILL YOU EXCEL IN YOUR ROLE?

• You try to add value to projects, in excess of what your instructions were.

• You are proactive, find things that need fixing and speak your mind, while also enjoying feedback and coaching from your team members.

• You enjoy optimizing workstreams and developing innovative solutions for getting to a stronger output with the same resources

• You consider yourself skilled at working with excel, as well as well-known, open-source LLMs and agent platforms.

• You have a continuously growing portfolio of tools, which you purposefully add to, such as for automation, modelling and related tasks, formerly executed manually in excel.

• You know you are, for now, a junior part of a larger team, but you want to become more impactful by taking on more responsibility and growing with the company (also full-time).

• You know your strengths, as well as your development areas and enjoy working on both with purpose.

WHAT DO WE OFFER?

• An in-office student job with 15-20 hours weekly, located at the Danish Technological Institute near Taastrup.

• A competitive salary as well as IT equipment and subscriptions provided to get your job done.

• A hands-on learning platform, working together with former senior executives and leadership from companies such as Novonesis, Ørsted, Topsoe, Saxo Bank, Cargill and AB Agri.

• Being part of an ambitious and diverse team, on track of an ambitious scaling journey in a competitive industry

For questions to the company, position and hiring process, you can contact Head of Finance/Chief of Staff Jascha Jäger under career@algiecel.com.

Site Compliance Lead

East Denmark: Hillerød, Bagsværd and Måløv

Your impact begins here

As Site Compliance Lead, you will help create fair, responsible and legally compliant working conditions across Novo Nordisk construction sites in East Denmark. You will bring clarity to complex compliance matters, strengthen consistent practices and help project teams manage risk effectively. By guiding operational activities and addressing irregularities with sound judgement, you will support compliant, efficient and sustainable project execution at our sites in Hillerød, Bagsværd and Måløv.

What you’ll bring

You combine strong Site Compliance expertise with the confidence to coordinate activities across teams, contractors and other stakeholders. You can assess complex information, make timely decisions and communicate requirements clearly, including when conversations are challenging.

• A relevant technical background, for example as a construction engineer, marine engineer or in a comparable field.

• Several years of relevant compliance experience, preferably from construction, large-scale projects, a regulated industry or a similar operational environment.

• Knowledge of labour relations, employment legislation, working environment requirements and the legal and regulatory context for construction activities.

• Experience with compliance monitoring, investigations, risk assessments and the management of non-compliance cases.

• Experience coordinating or leading employees, teams or operational activities.

• Professional working proficiency in Danish and English.

You will also need integrity, discretion and strong professional judgement. You are comfortable working independently, balancing changing priorities and escalating significant issues when required.

What you’ll do

• Ensure right staffing of Site Compliance Consultants and Safety Induction Consultants at our 3 construction locations in East Denmark, currently Hillerød, Bagsværd and Måløv.

• Coordinate onboarding and training of consultants, helping colleagues apply requirements consistently in their daily work.

• Monitor contractor performance, identify patterns and emerging risks, prepare timely reports.

• Help ensure that contractors, suppliers and their employees comply with applicable Danish labour legislation and Novo Nordisk Site Compliance requirements.

• Manage compliance breaches and irregularities, applying professional judgement to assess risk and determine appropriate next steps.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Site Compliance, a specialist function within API Environment, Health & Safety and Site Compliance that supports Novo’s construction sites in Denmark. The team helps projects meet relevant authority requirements, applicable legislation and internal standards while maintaining progress in project execution.

You will be reporting to the Head of Site Compliance, and your closest partners will include project organisations, Construction Health and Safety, Site Security, Category Owners, Communications, Project Management and other relevant site functions. You will also work directly with contractors and suppliers, bringing different perspectives together and creating clarity when requirements or priorities are complex.

What you can expect here

You will have the opportunity to shape how Site Compliance is delivered across major construction environments and to contribute directly to safer, fairer and more consistent ways of working. You will be trusted to use your expertise, take ownership and help colleagues solve compliance challenges. The department values collaboration, professionalism and a working environment in which people share knowledge and recognise collective progress.

Salary and Benefits

The Annual Base Salary for the role ranges from DKK 570,200 - 838,100, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

A competitive benefits package is offered, including a pension scheme (currently 13% employer contribution and 5% employee contribution) in accordance with the applicable Collective Agreement for Salaried Employees (Industriens Funktionæroverenskomst or “IFO”).

Benefits package also include a free choice account of currently 10% and 4% holiday allowance.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to strengthen responsible working conditions and consistent compliance across our construction sites, apply for the Site Compliance Lead role by 22 November 2026.

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. For questions, please reach out to Majken Balleby Jørgensen, EMJG@novonordisk.com.

**Head of Innovation, Director

**Can you turn scientific opportunities into meaningful innovation?

As Head of Innovation you will lead our innovation portfolio and early-stage innovation activities across R&D, turning scientific insight, clinical needs, and commercial opportunities into a focused pipeline of future products and technologies.

This is a Director-level individual contributor position, reporting directly to the VP R&D. The role has no direct reports and will lead through influence in a matrix organization, bringing together R&D, Upstream Product Management, Commercial Development and other functions to evaluate opportunities, make portfolio choices, and move the fittest ideas forward.

Every two seconds, Ferrosan Medical Devices’ products help surgeons and nurses control bleeding and avoid complications in surgical procedures. We make seconds count in surgical care, and we would love to have you join us in shaping what comes next.

**Shape our future innovation portfolio

**You will play a central role in identifying, assessing, and maturing new innovation opportunities. You will connect scientific and technical possibilities with unmet clinical needs, market potential, and our strategic priorities. A key part of your role will be to create focus: building a strong innovation portfolio and driving fact-based decisions on where to invest, what to advance, and when to stop.

**Your role

**As Head of Innovation, you will:

• Lead the R&D innovation portfolio, setting priorities and driving clear decisions on where to explore, invest, accelerate, partner, or stop

• Mobilize and motivate scientists and engineers across our competence centers, creating commitment and bringing the right expertise together to advance innovation opportunities in a matrix organization

• Connect science, clinical needs, and commercial potential, translating insights into compelling innovation opportunities and business rationales

• Build and leverage our external innovation ecosystem, engaging with start-ups, academia, research institutions, and MedTech/Pharma companies to identify technologies and develop strategic partnerships

• Create alignment and visibility around the innovation pipeline, communicating priorities, progress, risks, and recommendations to R&D and senior leadership

**Qualifications

**Ideally, you bring:

• MSc or PhD in biomaterials, chemistry, material sciences, biomedical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related field

• Advanced user of AI-enabled ways of working, including generative and agentic AI, with the ability to apply these tools practically to accelerate research, analysis, knowledge synthesis, and innovation

• Proven experience in the development of Class III medical devices or combination products, ideally including exposure to the US PMA pathway

• Strong track record in driving innovation and complex R&D programs, from early opportunities through feasibility and development

• Strong matrix leader, able to mobilize and motivate scientists, engineers, and cross-functional teams without formal authority

• Highly structured and concise thinker, able to synthesize complex scientific and technical topics and communicate clear conclusions and recommendations to senior stakeholders

The position is based at our headquarters in Søborg, Copenhagen. We welcome international candidates willing to relocate.

**Some of the facts and a little piece of history

**Ferrosan Medical Devices develops and produces a portfolio of medical devices used in surgical care. Our portfolio consists of various hemostatic products to minimize bleeding challenges in surgery and electromechanical medical devices to perform breast biopsies. We are an international company with products registered in more than 100 countries. Our products are marketed in collaboration with global medtech partners. New ideas are developed and matured from the first thought to finished implementation in production. And we manage the business with an uncompromising focus on quality based on current GMP requirements.

**Interested?

**Please submit your cover letter, CV, and any relevant supporting materials by 30 November 2026. We will review applications on an ongoing basis and encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

As Process Scientist/Engineer, you will be the go-to person for laboratory equipment, processes and technical know-how in our QC laboratories in Kalundborg. You will keep equipment reliable and compliant, and help shape Laboratory Service, a newly established unit with clear owner-ship of shared laboratory support. When instruments perform as they should, your colleagues can test with confidence, supporting the production of insulin and GLP-1 for people living with diabetes and obesity.

What you’ll bring

You work independently, take ownership and enjoy making laboratory practice better, one prac-tical improvement at a time.

· A bachelor’s or master’s degree in natural sciences, engineering, pharmacology or a related field – or equivalent experience as a laboratory technician with strong equipment compe-tence.

· Experience with laboratory equipment, such as HPLC/UPLC or other analytical instruments, including qualification, calibration and maintenance.

· Experience with QMS work, such as deviations, change requests and documentation.

· An interest in automation, digitalisation and new technologies.

· Fluent English, written and spoken.

· A curious, can-do mindset, a sharp eye for practical improvements, and the ability to stay calm and keep the overview when priorities change.

· Strong communication skills and a natural ability to build relationships across teams and de-partments.

Useful, but not essential:

· Experience in a GMP-regulated environment.

· Experience with Lean/cLEAN and project work.

· Danish language skills. Much of our collaboration happens in Danish, so good communica-tion in both languages is an advantage.

What you’ll do

You will make sure laboratory equipment supports stable daily operations, with the right bal-ance of quality, cost, environment and delivery.

· Take professional responsibility for the equipment lifecycle, from idea and purchase to maintenance, replacement and retirement.

· Secure qualification, calibration, QMS support and up-to-date equipment documentation in line with GMP requirements.

· Support the laboratories proactively, so equipment and daily operations deliver the right output in the right quality.

· Handle vendor dialogue and coordinate service agreements (SLAs) together with the team.

· Give input to capacity planning, projects and the future equipment strategy.

· Lead and take part in cross-functional initiatives that optimise and automate existing pro-cesses and equipment.

· Share knowledge and best practices across laboratories, sites and teams, and challenge ex-isting processes in a respectful and constructive way.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Laboratory Service team in Kalundborg, part of Global Quality Control and an-chored in QC Business Operations. The team brings together shared laboratory support activi-ties that previously sat across different QC units. The aim is clear ownership of laboratory equip-ment, infrastructure and shared services, and stronger standardisation, flexibility and use of our capabilities across laboratories. The first priority is to keep operations running and support strategic initiatives for equipment and facilities.

Your colleagues are professionals and laboratory technicians who work close to the equipment, so you stay in close contact with the laboratory users who rely on it every day. You will also work with vendors and with colleagues across laboratories, sites and teams. Your manager is Helle Bülow Mindegaard Christensen.

Kalundborg is a city within the city: about 3,000 colleagues across several factories, one hour’s drive from Copenhagen. Here we produce insulin and GLP-1 and work at the forefront of tech-nology, systems, methods and processes. In Enterprise IT & Quality, colleagues work across the Novo value chain, stay close to stakeholders and help deliver trusted technology, high quality and responsible ways of working.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take ownership in a dynamic workday where priorities change and results come from working things out together. You will build new skills through project work, automa-tion and digital initiatives, and by sharing practice across sites. You will have the chance to speak up, contribute your expertise and help shape how a new unit works.

Not every ambition comes true, but if you want to become a specialist, a project lead or a man-ager one day, this role can be your way there.

Join Copenhagen Energy Trading as our new Machine Learning Engineer

Machine learning is becoming an increasingly important part of how we understand energy markets, improve forecasts, and make trading decisions. We are therefore looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to move our models from research to production, building robust, scalable pipelines that continuously improve our strategies.

At Copenhagen Energy Trading (CET), we combine deep market expertise with machine learning, quantitative research, data, and engineering to automate and optimise how we trade power. We’re a small, highly ambitious team based in central Copenhagen, specialising in power trading and asset management across Europe and North America. Technology is at the core of how we operate, supported by one of Europe’s most advanced automated and analytical trading environments for power markets.

The Opportunity

Energy markets produce vast amounts of data and are continuously shaped by weather, power production, transmission constraints, and market behaviour. Using that data meaningfully requires accurate models and reliable software and infrastructure that allow those models to run in production.

As our Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll work across machine learning and software development. Alongside quantitative researchers, software engineers and traders, you’ll build the production systems behind our ML pipelines, making our trading more performant, more reliable and more automated.

You’ll own the full lifecycle around the model: from data management to the pipelines and frameworks that deploy and monitor our models, keeping them reliable and adaptive as markets evolve. The opportunity for impact is large, and so is what it asks of you: dedication, real talent and the willingness to grind through hard problems. This is a hands-on engineering role at the centre of how CET uses machine learning to trade.

What You Will Do

• Strengthen our ML framework: Build and improve the framework our researchers use to build models and quantitative strategies.

• Build production-ready software: Design and develop reliable, scalable, and well-tested Python software that integrates machine learning into our internal trading platforms.

• Develop data infrastructure: Build and maintain data pipelines and storage solutions for ingesting, transforming, and serving diverse market and fundamental data.

• Ship and operate models: Take models from experiment to production, including deployment, serving, monitoring and experiment tracking

• Improve our ML and engineering practices: Help strengthen our approach to MLOps, testing, CI/CD, code reviews, and the wider model development lifecycle.

• Shape our technical solutions: Evaluate and introduce tools and technologies that improve how we develop, deploy, and operate machine learning solutions.

• Collaborate across disciplines: Work closely with quantitative researchers, traders, and software engineers to turn business and market needs into practical technical solutions.

• Build energy-market expertise: Develop a deep understanding of power markets and how machine learning, data, and software can improve trading decisions.

What We're Looking For

We value strong technical ability, sound judgement, curiosity, and motivation to learn. While we don't expect a perfect match, many of the following qualifications will help you succeed in the role:

• Strong software engineering skills: Experience building clean, scalable, tested, and production-ready software. Strong Python skills are essential, as Python is our primary development language.

• MLOps and development practices: Proficiency in Git, code reviews, CI/CD, experiment tracking, model deployment, and monitoring.

• Cloud computing: Experience with Azure, AWS, or GCP, ideally including relevant data and machine learning services.

• Problem-solving and communication: The ability to structure complex problems, communicate clearly, and collaborate with colleagues across technical and commercial disciplines. Full professional proficiency in English is required.

• Ownership: The ability to work independently and deliver in a fast-paced environment.

• Interest in energy markets: Curiosity about power markets, trading, and energy systems. Previous experience in energy or trading is an advantage, but not a requirement.

• Education: A degree with a strong technical focus, e.g., Computer Science, Software Engineering, or other relevant fields. We welcome different educational backgrounds and levels of qualification.

What We Offer

• Growth environment: Become part of a young, ambitious, and expanding tech-driven trading company where talented people are given responsibility and room to grow.

• Exceptional team: Work closely with experienced quantitative researchers, software engineers and power traders.

• Competitive compensation: Receive a competitive salary package and attractive benefits that reflect your skills and contributions.

• Strong culture: Participate in both social and professional events, including team sports, company parties, team-building, and informal gatherings that strengthen our team spirit.

• Central Copenhagen location: Work from our office in Carlsberg Byen, located in beautifully renovated historic Carlsberg buildings.

How to Apply

If this opportunity feels like the right fit for you, we would love to hear from you.

Please apply via LinkedIn and submit your cover letter, CV, and university transcripts as a single PDF. Please note that applications that do not meet these requirements may not be considered.

Application deadline: November 27, 2026

If you have any questions, please contact Carl Frederik Grønvald (Senior Quantitative Analyst) at cfg@copenhagen-energy.com or Anna Schumann (People & Culture Manager) at as@copenhagen-energy.com.

About us

Trustpilot began in 2007 with a simple yet powerful idea that is more relevant today than ever — to be the universal symbol of trust, bringing consumers and businesses together through reviews. Trustpilot is open, independent, and impartial — we help consumers make the right choices and businesses to build trust, grow and improve.

Today, we have more than 350 million reviews and 60 million monthly active users across the globe, with 149 billion annual Trustpilot brand impressions, and the numbers keep growing. We have more than 1000 employees and we’re headquartered in Copenhagen, with operations in  Amsterdam, Denver, Edinburgh, Hamburg, London, Melbourne, Milan and New York.

We’re driven by connection. It’s at the heart of what we do. Our culture keeps things fresh –– it’s built on the relationships we create. We talk, we laugh, we collaborate and we respect each other. jobs.description:
Most companies that do conferencing hand you one slice of it. The desktop app, or the media pipeline, or, maybe, the join flow. Everything else you pass over a wall to another team. Not in this case. One team owns the whole path across the Airtame platform: Airtame 3, Airtame Go, Virtual Airtame, and browser, desktop, and mobile apps that go with them. The bar remains at an effortless experience. Someone walks into a room, and starts sharing. No app to hunt for, no login to chase.

The team is four engineers, and we're hiring their technical and people lead: someone who spends about 60% of time hands-on with the hardest problems, and the rest growing the engineers around them.

**About Airtame

**We're around 55 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, and you'd work from there or remotely from within the EU. We make the hardware and the software that runs on it, so a call you make about the streaming stack ends up in a product bolted to a wall in meeting rooms around the world. The team is small, works across disciplines, and reaches a global market from a small base.

Year one outcomes

Make joining a call one step that works. Today, getting an authenticated meeting started from a room takes too many turns: personal logins, manual entry, a different quirk on every platform. A year from now, starting a scheduled call on Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, or Webex should be something a room just does. Judge it by how often it works on the first try, and how rarely it reaches support.

Take the friction out of screen sharing. The browser path loses first-time users: too many clicks, not enough signposting. You'll own getting a newcomer from a short code to their screen on the wall without a stumble, and getting Miracast and AirPlay stable enough to turn on by default.

Make it behave the same everywhere. The experience varies between Airtame 3, Virtual Airtame, browser, desktop, and mobile today. By year-end, sharing and calling should feel like one product no matter which surface you're on, with real-time quality that holds up on whatever network the room happens to have.

Lead the team. You'll run the 1:1s, set the technical bar, and support team members' growth. The measure is simple: a year in, the team runs on your leadership day to day.

Push AI-assisted development further. The team already builds with AI daily. You'll lead the next step: sharper workflows, better tooling choices, new patterns that make the whole group faster. By year-end, the team's AI practices should be visibly ahead of where they started.

Who you are

• The player-coach. You've owned a team's technical direction: the architecture calls, the reviews where the hard problems get caught. And you want the people side too. Growing engineers, running 1:1s, hiring. You're not looking to trade one for the other. Maybe you've been a staff engineer or tech lead ready to own a team, or a manager who never stopped building. Either way, 60/40 sounds about right to you.

• Comfortable across the stack. Real-time media is second nature to you: WebRTC, streaming, the way audio and video behave over a network you don't control. You've gone deep somewhere, whether a media pipeline, native protocols, or a cross-platform client, and you can hold your own everywhere else, on browser, desktop, and mobile.

• You've made stubborn systems cooperate. Half this job is getting software to play nicely with platforms you don't own: Teams, Zoom, Meet, Webex, the operating system's own media APIs, each with its own idea of how things should go. You've done that kind of integration, and you keep your head when every platform behaves differently.

• You measure yourself by the room. Your bar is the person standing at the "share" button. Someone who's never seen an Airtame, getting their screen up first try with no help. That's what you optimize for, and it steers the calls you make when something has to give.

• You use AI as a daily tool. You write code with it, debug with it, prototype with it. You've formed your own view on where it speeds things up and where it gets in the way, and you help the people around you do the same.

**Logistics

**Location: Remote in Europe, or hybrid from our Copenhagen office.

Employment type: Full-time preferred. We're also open to a project-based contract scoped to delivering the native protocol implementations.

****Why Airtame:

• The defining calls are still ahead. Airtame's collaboration software keeps spreading across more devices and form factors, so the shape of the next phase is still open, and you'd be the one setting it.

• At our size, a major call you make shows up in front of customers within weeks, so the feedback comes back fast.

• A healthy work-life balance.

• Significant responsibility and ownership over projects and your field of expertise.

• Five weeks paid vacation and 5 days of extra paid AirtameFlex days.

• Flexible work environment, with a hybrid mindset.

• Pension and private health insurance (on FTE Copenhagen contract).

Airtame is an equal opportunity employer. We have colleagues across the globe, with both in-office and full-time remote workers. This feeds into our international hybrid mindset, with people from 25+ nationalities that make up the Airtame team.

Our work-life cultural balance is key to our success. Our team encompasses our values of trust and open communication to support each other and to collaborate in a fun and collective way.

****What Our Employment Decisions Are NOT Based On

****Race, colour, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, disability, ethnicity, national origin, marital status, family or parental status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other legally protected classification or status. And we will not tolerate discrimination or harassment.

****What Our Employment Decisions ARE Based On

****Business needs, job requirements, individual qualifications, and candidates potential for growing with Airtame.

****How We Handle Your Application Data

****Airtame ApS (CVR 35478973, Copenhagen), together with Airtame US Inc. for US roles, processes the information you submit to assess your application. We do this under the EU General Data Protection Regulation, wherever you are based. Your data is stored in Greenhouse, our recruiting system, which may store it outside the EU under standard EU safeguards. Only the people involved in hiring can see it. For roles with privileged access to our systems, we’ll contact one professional reference or previous employer that you name, to confirm your role and dates. We’ll tell you before we do. We keep your data for 6 months after the recruitment process ends, or longer where US law requires it or where you consent to us keeping it for future roles. To get a copy of your data, correct or delete it, or object to how we use it, write to data@airtame.com. You can also complain to the Danish Data Protection Agency (Datatilsynet).

****Business needs, job requirements, individual qualifications, and candidates potential for growing with Airtame.
